title: AI-designed SARS-CoV-2 variants escape prevalent antibodies

content_html:
While headlines warn that AI could unleash future biological threats, the technology also offers our best defense: a way to anticipate viral evolution and stress-test treatments. Rather than waiting for SARS-CoV-2 to mutate and outrun our immune system, my colleagues and I at École Normale Supérieure and Institut Pasteur built EscapeMap. Published in Cell Systems, our framework generates highly mutated, functional viral proteins to evaluate therapeutics against future evolutionary trajectories long before those mutations surface in the real world.

Strikingly, most of our AI-generated variants escaped prevalent antibodies, demonstrating that our evolutionary struggle with SARS-CoV-2 is far from over.

Model architecture: Combining evolutionary data and biophysics

For a new viral variant to spread successfully in the real world, it must strike a delicate balance between remaining structurally stable, retaining strong binding to human ACE2 receptors and evading host antibodies. EscapeMap evaluates the likelihood of potential viral variants by combining three distinct, complementary modules.

First, the Sequence Viability module uses an unsupervised generative AI model—a Restricted Boltzmann Machine—trained on pre-pandemic coronavirus sequences. It learns the co-evolutionary rules that dictate how different parts of the viral protein must work together to maintain its physical shape and structural stability. Second, the Receptor Affinity module uses a thermodynamic model calibrated with experimental scanning data to estimate how tightly the virus binds to human host cells. Third, the Immune Selection module incorporates antibody screening panels to model immune pressure—the collective evolutionary force exerted by antibodies that forces the virus to adapt or perish.

Predicting the next mutations

By tracking how immune pressure shifted over the course of the pandemic, EscapeMap reveals how human immunity drives viral exploration. Following widespread vaccination and booster doses, population antibody diversity expanded significantly. EscapeMap captured this shift as a mutational explosion, where antibody escape becomes the dominant evolutionary force pushing the virus into previously unexplored sequence territory.

Experimental validation: In vitro testing of artificial variants

To test whether the framework could design realistic, functional viral proteins, we used EscapeMap to generate 22 artificial viral proteins. These sequences were computationally engineered to escape broadly neutralizing antibodies SA55, S2E12, S309 and VIR-7229.

Despite carrying up to 25 amino acid substitutions relative to the original Wuhan-Hu-1 strain, 11 of the 22 designed variants expressed as stable, functional proteins in laboratory assays. This 50% success rate represents a massive leap over random mutagenesis, which yields functional proteins less than 2% of the time at comparable mutational distances. Only the broad neutralizer VIR-7229 retained strong binding across all tested variants. Conversely, we identified a single substitution, G504E, that completely abolishes SA55 neutralization across both the wild type and the modern KP.3 variant of concern.

Beyond SARS-CoV-2: Proactive therapeutic design

By generating diverse antigen libraries, researchers can now "stress-test" therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and vaccine candidates against computationally designed viral variants years in advance. Beyond monoclonal treatments, this generative strategy offers a roadmap for broad-spectrum vaccine development. Designing mosaic nanoparticles co-displaying AI-generated viral variants can help focus human immune responses onto universally conserved epitopes, paving the way for resilient vaccines against future sarbecovirus threats.

content_html_zh:
虽然头条新闻警告人工智能可能会引发未来的生物威胁，但该技术也为我们提供了最好的防御：一种预测病毒进化和压力测试治疗的方法。 我和我在巴黎高等师范学院和巴斯德研究所的同事们并没有等待 SARS-CoV-2 发生变异并超越我们的免疫系统，而是创建了 EscapeMap。 我们的框架发表在《细胞系统》上，可以生成高度突变的功能性病毒蛋白，以便早在这些突变出现在现实世界之前就根据未来的进化轨迹评估治疗方法。

引人注目的是，我们大多数人工智能生成的变体都逃脱了普遍的抗体，这表明我们与 SARS-CoV-2 的进化斗争还远未结束。

模型架构：结合进化数据和生物物理学

为了让新的病毒变种在现实世界中成功传播，它必须在保持结构稳定、保持与人类 ACE2 受体的强结合和逃避宿主抗体之间取得微妙的平衡。 EscapeMap 通过组合三个不同的互补模块来评估潜在病毒变异的可能性。

首先，序列可行性模块使用无监督的生成人工智能模型——受限玻尔兹曼机——根据大流行前的冠状病毒序列进行训练。 它学习共同进化规则，这些规则决定病毒蛋白的不同部分必须如何协同工作以维持其物理形状和结构稳定性。 其次，受体亲和力模块使用根据实验扫描数据校准的热力学模型来估计病毒与人类宿主细胞结合的紧密程度。 第三，免疫选择模块结合了抗体筛选面板来模拟免疫压力——抗体施加的集体进化力量，迫使病毒适应或灭亡。

预测下一个突变

通过跟踪免疫压力在大流行过程中如何变化，EscapeMap 揭示了人类免疫如何推动病毒探索。 在广泛接种疫苗和加强剂量之后，群体抗体多样性显着扩大。 EscapeMap 将这种转变捕获为突变爆炸，其中抗体逃逸成为主导进化力量，将病毒推入先前未探索的序列领域。

实验验证：人工变体的体外测试

为了测试该框架是否可以设计出真实的、功能性的病毒蛋白，我们使用 EscapeMap 生成了 22 种人工病毒蛋白。 这些序列经过计算设计，可逃避广泛中和抗体 SA55、S2E12、S309 和 VIR-7229。

尽管相对于原始的 Wuu-Hu-1 菌株进行了多达 25 个氨基酸取代，但 22 个设计的变体中有 11 个在实验室检测中表达为稳定的功能性蛋白质。 50% 的成功率代表着相对于随机诱变的巨大飞跃，在相当的突变距离下，随机诱变产生功能性蛋白质的几率不到 2%。 只有广泛的中和剂 VIR-7229 在所有测试的变体中保持了强结合。 相反，我们发现了一个单一取代 G504E，它完全消除了野生型和现代 KP.3 变体中的 SA55 ​​中和作用。

超越 SARS-CoV-2：主动治疗设计

通过生成不同的抗原库，研究人员现在可以提前数年针对计算设计的病毒变体对治疗性单克隆抗体和候选疫苗进行“压力测试”。 除了单克隆治疗之外，这种生成策略还为广谱疫苗的开发提供了路线图。 设计共同展示人工智能生成的病毒变体的镶嵌纳米颗粒可以帮助将人类免疫反应集中在普遍保守的表位上，从而为针对未来沙病毒威胁的弹性疫苗铺平道路。
